author: Harry
text:
dcabfx wrote:... I don't see that on my H4. Nothing to worry about though. We work with what we got....

this is a problem when you quickly scan the charts in a HTF. ideally when you identify something important breaking (your SR as i call it in FLs) you have to dig into the LTFs to find its exact limits. you will be amazed how many times you will mark something say in H1, price will come to it and think it engulfed it but then you go and find the exact limits of that FL in the LTF and you see it didnt and your small almost invisible FL worked perfectly well.

it doesnt mean that because something doesnt show up in HTFs it is not significant

author: madwt
text:
Harry wrote:

dcabfx wrote:... I don't see that on my H4. Nothing to worry about though. We work with what we got....

this is a problem when you quickly scan the charts in a HTF. ideally when you identify something important breaking (your SR as i call it in FLs) you have to dig into the LTFs to find its exact limits. you will be amazed how many times you will mark something say in H1, price will come to it and think it engulfed it but then you go and find the exact limits of that FL in the LTF and you see it didnt and your small almost invisible FL worked perfectly well.

it doesnt mean that because something doesnt show up in HTFs it is not significant

This is something I have been meaning to post for a while.... and it seems now is a good time.

Harry makes a great point here and it's very important to grasp.

I have seen many charts marked on the HTF with a FL and then the engulf is shown. Sometimes it looks like the engulf does not work as price continues to charge on. Its worth your time looking at every FL on the LTF and asking yourself where the true limit of the FL is and hence what price level needs to be breached to constitute an engulf. As we are basing our understanding of what price is doing on the engulf of a price level, this is something worth pondering.

Here is an example. It is not a great example as it's the first one I looked, but it's sufficient to illustrate the point, and the question to ask yourself while conducting your homework.

I realise it's a pretty crappy example... so here is a sightly better one.

Note: I am not saying which is right.. I am still learning. I am only pointing out its a question to ask,

author: DrSwing
text: This is a great question to ask madwt. I have pondered this issue many times and have no definitive answer. So to solve this issue in my trading, I look for charts that have very clean definite FLs and pass up on the types that you have posted above. It doesn't answer the question though!

author: Harry
text:
absolutely Madwt

very often what you see in the HTFs as an FL (in the shape of a rbr/dbd) is the reaction to the LTF original one.

i think i have drawn this somewhere in this thread, how an LTF original FL and its subsequent returns translate into the FL(s) you would see in the HTFs. or if not you have have a go and draw it here.

make no mistake, unless the true FL breaks there is no break. so always dig down to find the true limits of it
